Fig: 5.1.2 Bishazari Tal BOTANICAL GARDEN (EX-SITU CONSERVATION) Botanical gardens are large areas dedicated to growing various types of plants for scientific and educational purposes. The idea of botanical gardens dates back to Theophrastus, but modern botanical gardens have evolved significantly. In addition to outdoor plants, they now include greenhouses, research laboratories, libraries, and herbariums with documented collections of different plant species. The International Association of Botanic Gardens (IABG), established in 1962, plays a crucial role in coordinating research and facilitating the exchange of plant materials. Importance of Botanical Gardens:

a) Botanical gardens provide living plant materials essential for systematic studies. b) They cultivate important plants from the local area. c) Botanical gardens maintain records of the local flora. d) They supply seeds and materials for various botanical research activities. e) Botanical gardens grow and preserve rare and endangered plant species.
f) They cultivate and maintain plants that wouldn't naturally grow during certain seasons by regulating greenhouse temperatures.

Botanical gardens (BG) in Nepal a) Brindavan Botanical Garden, Hetauda b) Devariya Botanical Garden, Kailali c) Dhanushadham Botanical Garden, Janakpur d) Dhitachaur Botanical Garden, Jumla e) Daman Botanical Garden, Makwanpur f) Dhakeri Botanical Garden, Banke g) Mai pokhari Botanical Garden, Ilam h) Mulpani Botanical Garden, Salyan i) National Botanical Garden, Godawari j) Tistung Botanical Garden, Makwanpur k) World peace Botanical Garden, Pokhara Fig: 5.1.3 National botanical garden, Godawari, Lalitpur SEED BANK (EX-SITU CONSERVATION) A seed bank or germplasm bank is a location where specific conditions are upheld to safeguard seeds from various plant species, whether they are wild or cultivated. The main goal is straightforward: to secure the long-term preservation of a wide variety of plants for future generations. Originally, they were created for important food crops, but now they also store seeds of many endangered wild plants. These seeds can stay dormant for thousands of years if kept at a low temperature (below -5°C) and humidity. They include major crop plants such as cereals, soyabean, cotton and many vegetable species. A challenge in a seed bank is making sure the seeds stay alive. Periodic tests are conducted on seed samples to check their ability to sprout. If the germination capability drops below an acceptable level, around 85%, new seeds are produced by growing the stored seeds and then harvesting them for storage.

The importance of seed bank The undeniable and significant threat of species extinction, caused by both natural factors and human activities, poses a serious risk to our planet. Once a species disappears, it is lost forever. Seed banks play a crucial role in addressing this threat, particularly for plants. They are integral to a strong seed system that ensures food security.
1. The importance of seed banks includes preserving the genes necessary for plant breeders to enhance crop yield, disease resistance, drought tolerance, nutritional quality, and more.
2. Additionally, seed banks help prevent the loss of genetic diversity in rare plant species, contributing to the conservation of biodiversity outside their natural habitats (ex-situ).
